title: $7,500/yr for 40 Years (The Number Gets Ridiculous)
subtitle: Most people max the Roth for 30 years. Almost nobody for 40. The difference: $1.5 million vs $708K. The last decade does the work.
source_irs: Compound math; contribution phaseout (no phaseout) under IRC §219(g)

concepts.heading: The Math
concepts.lede: Put $7,500 a year into a Roth for 40 years at 7% real return. The end value: $1,497,000, all tax-free.
body: Real return: 7% per year. Compounded annually.

concepts.heading: The Last Decade Does the Work
concepts.lede: From year 30 to year 40, the balance more than doubles. The last ten years add $789,000 — more than the first 30 added combined.
body: Years 30-40 add: $789,000 — more than the $708,000 the first 30 years added.
The last decade is more than the first three combined. Compounding is back-loaded.

concepts.heading: The Trade
concepts.lede: To get 40 years of $7,500, you have to start at 22 and not stop until 62. The cost: $300,000 of post-tax dollars over 40 years.
body: Pre-tax equivalent: $300K Roth ≈ $400K pre-tax at 25% bracket.
That's ~3.7× growth on the pre-tax dollars, vs. ~3× in a brokerage after cap-gains drag.
